documents.title: Bambu Filament Technical Data Sheet V3.0: PLA Translucent
Bambu PLA Translucent Safety Data Sheet SDS20250928A17
Bambu Lab Filament Hex Code Table: PLA Translucent
Filament guide: printer, nozzle, AMS, build plate and glue compatibility

notes: Mechanical keys hold the TDS X-Y printed-specimen values; the registry has one key per scope, so the Z values (tensile 28.9 ± 4 MPa, elongation 9.6 ± 1.7 %, bending modulus 2650 ± 140 MPa, bending strength 42 ± 4 MPa, impact 8.5 ± 1.2 kJ/m²) are not stored. Density, melting, glass transition, Vicat and HDT come from the TDS "Physical Properties" table (ISO 1183, DSC, ISO 306, ISO 75; the specimen form is not stated) and sit under material.* / thermal.*, apart from the printed-specimen mechanical.* rows. The registry has no *.printed / *.material key pair, so the split is by key group and test_condition.

TDS facts not stored as spec rows (no registry key, or one row per key): Young's modulus (X-Y 2880 ± 190 MPa, Z 2550 ± 150 MPa), melt index (4.08 ± 1.5 g/10 min at 210 °C, 2.16 kg), crystallization temperature ("/"), the second heat deflection row (60 ℃ at 0.45 MPa; the 1.8 MPa row is stored, as for the other filaments), saturated water absorption rate (0.34% at 25 °C, 55% RH), printing and storage humidity (< 20% RH, sealed, with desiccant), nozzle size (0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 mm; recorded as a compatible_with relation only, since the sources disagree on 0.2 mm), bed surface preparation (glue), retraction length (0.6 - 1.0 mm) and speed (20 - 40 mm/s), chamber temperature (25 - 45°C), max overhang angle (55 °), max bridging length (30 mm), spool material (ABS, temperature resistance 70 °C), spool size (diameter 200 mm, height 67 mm), annealing of prints (50 to 60 °C for 6 to 12 hours), and the odor, skin hazard, chemical stability, solubility, chemical resistance, flammability and combustion product rows.
The TDS recommended chamber temperature (25 - 45°C) is not written to thermal.chamber_temp: that key is a printer capability, not a filament print setting.

material.spool_type is not written: the store page's Type group has one value ("Filament with spool") and no spool bullet, and the TDS gives the spool material (ABS) and size, not a spool type name; a text composed from those two rows would not be a spool type and would feed the spool_type facet mirror. It is not marked not_published either, since the TDS does describe the spool.

SDS facts not stored: product name "Bambu PLA Translucent"; the model designation "A17-xx" ("xx stands for any suffix"), a code pattern rather than one model, so identity.model is not written (as for the other filaments; the store page's own identity.model row is "PLA Translucent", which an official_doc value would replace); CLP "Not classified", no PBT/vPvB substance or endocrine disruptor, and "Not hazardous goods" for sea (IMDG), DOT, road (ADR/RID) and air (ICAO-TI) transport. Its section 9 "No data available" for melting point and density does not override the TDS values.

Source disagreements kept for review: nozzle temperature (TDS 200 - 240 °C vs material-table wiki generic PLA* row 190 - 240 ±10 °C); oven drying temperature (TDS and the PLA wiki row "PLA CF / Translucent" 50 °C vs material-table wiki generic PLA row 55 ℃); 0.2 mm nozzle (the TDS lists it under Nozzle Size and the generic wiki rows allow it; the store FAQ and the PLA wiki tip exclude the 0.2 mm stainless steel nozzle). The product TDS values are kept for the spec keys; for the 0.2 mm nozzle both statements are kept as relations (compatible_with the TDS list "0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 mm nozzles"; not_compatible_with "Hotend with Stainless Steel Nozzle 0.2 mm").

Heatbed and AMS drying (no key; oven values are stored): TDS X1 Series printer heatbed 60 - 70 °C, 12 h; PLA wiki hot bed 70℃，12 h and AMS HT / AMS 2 Pro 55℃，8 h; material-table wiki generic PLA row 45 ℃ for 12 h in the AMS 2 Pro and AMS HT, drying before use "Recommended", desiccant during use "Optional". The store FAQ says "Dry before use to ensure the best print quality and consistent finish."

Build plate guidance: the TDS lists glue as the bed surface preparation and the material-table wiki recommends glue stick or liquid glue (and marks the Engineering Plate "Glue Required" for generic PLA); this is a recommendation, and the Engineering Plate is not in the TDS plate list, so no requires relation and no Engineering Plate relation is written. The store page bullet "Clean Build Plates Before Printing" is a usage instruction, not a relation.

Marketing prose proves no number: "enhanced durability", "Durable for Long-Term Use", "greater impact and aging resistance compared to generic translucent PLA", "frosted finish diffuses light beautifully" and "more beginner-friendly than PETG Translucent" are not stored as values or relations. "Bonds with All PLA Filaments" (Product Features › bullet 2) is a compatibility statement and is stored as the relation compatible_with "All PLA Filaments".

Hex: all 10 store colours have exactly one hex cell, matched by the colour name without the code in parentheses. The TDS and the store page both say "available in 10 vibrant colors", which matches the 10 Colour values.

The store page links a "Filament RoHS" certificate (https://store.bblcdn.com/s7/default/369b7d0c17804f9d8a4402a121dd8d1d/Bambu_PLA_Translucent_RoHS.pdf) that was not cached and not read, so safety.certifications is neither curated nor marked not_published.

The store page links its "printing tips on WIKI" to https://wiki.bambulab.com/en/knowledge-sharing/transparent-petg (a PETG page), which was not cached and not read. The PLA wiki's own transparency section (5.2) was read instead.
material.diameter_tolerance (± 0.03 mm) is the store page's own row (Product Features › bullet 4); the TDS gives no tolerance, so it is not restated here and not marked not_published.

No in-the-box list: no official packing list exists for this filament (the store page has no What's in the Box section). No requires relation for a spool: the only Type value is "Filament with spool".
The store FAQ (5.Safety Tips) says the filament is not food-grade and the PLA wiki says PLA filaments other than PLA Pure are not food-contact grade; no registry key holds this.
not_published lists only filament keys (registry appliesTo includes "filament"); the generic logistics and printer keys with an empty appliesTo are not marked for a filament.
